newsitem.title: USA: Ohio lawmaker offers tax effort index for schools.
newsitem.headline: Ohio lawmaker offers tax effort index for schools.

text.p: An Ohio lawmaker unveiled a tax effort index for school districts Friday that his aide said could be used to help the state shape a new funding system next year.

Jamey Gray, a legislative aide to State Rep. Gene Krebs, R-Camden, said with education funding looking to be the top issue to be tackled by Ohio lawmakers next year, the index would be helpful in indentifying which districts "are more deserving of state assistance."

Krebs, in a news release, said that "by measuring tax effort, we can take the first step in identifying those school districts that are really trying hard to provide their children with the best educational opportunities, but still cannot make ends meet."

According to the release, a district's tax effort index was determined by dividing the millage rate by the product of property valuation per pupil, the percent of that value that is not exempt or abated and the income per pupil.

Although local news reports indicate that lawmakers said they will focus on education funding next year, they may be forced to do so if the Ohio Supreme Court rules the state's school funding system is unconstitutional.

The state's high court is expected to rule next month in a case brought by five Ohio school districts. While the trial court found the funding system unconstitutional, a state appeals court overturned that decision.
